title: Buddy, the quiet kid brother he barely knew
summary: Monk and Buddy never bonded growing up, and Buddy felt sidelined when Monk and Wes returned.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, Wes was still working a day job and playing, too, wasn't he?
Wes was working two day jobs and playing, at one point. I'd like to touch upon a little thing here, where I passed by without mentioning Buddy came into the...
When did he get to be old enough, and how did he start playing?
Well, like I said, Buddy and I...our earlier age in life, we didn't really come together.
Well, you didn't live together for a long time.

Yeah. It was like, and it was for both of us...When I moved back to Indianapolis to stay with my mother, and Buddy was there, at the age of about 11 when I was 19, approaching 20, we didn't have anything in common at all. No more than the fact that he was my kid brother, which was fine. I didn't know how to hang out with him, talk to him or...And he was like...Bud is, was always, a withdrawn person and...no question, because...

Yeah, right. And he just by nature is a very quiet person. When we moved into Indianapolis, Wes and I came over. My mother showed us so much attention because she was so happy we were home again. I guess what happened was, I can see now

how it could easily have affected Buddy, because in order to show us all the attention, it didn't give him...And he needed it worse at that age. It was...somebody had...Wes...It was like we had invaded upon his thing when we came in.

It was all Wes and me, me and Wes, because the next door neighbors, all our relatives and everybody was coming around. It was Monk and Wes, because we were back home again. But then Buddy was thrown to the wayside there, a little bit, more than a youngster at that age should be. Which I'm sure nobody really meant it that way.
